scenes.title: You can start here
scenes.visual: A diverse founder sits at a desk in a contemporary Dubai workspace, looking at a blank notebook.
scenes.narration: You do not need a perfect idea to start. You need curiosity and a willingness to learn. Welcome to LYNQ Venture Studio Academy. This journey helps you turn questions into practical steps.

scenes.title: Notice a real problem
scenes.visual: An event visitor searches handwritten contact notes after a networking event.
scenes.narration: A venture begins with someone’s problem. Imagine an event visitor who cannot reconnect with a person they met. First understand that experience. Choosing an app comes later.

scenes.title: Know your starting point
scenes.visual: Close-ups of a notebook, calendar, and a founder reflecting.
scenes.narration: Your experience is useful. Maybe you organise events, support customers, or understand a community. Write down what you bring, what you still need to learn, and why building a venture matters to you.

scenes.title: Learn by doing
scenes.visual: Editable five-stage roadmap added in post-production over clean navy background.
scenes.narration: Across Discover, Validate, Build, Launch, and Scale, you will watch, learn, build, ask for guidance, challenge assumptions, and complete practical work. Finishing lessons does not prove that a business will succeed.

scenes.title: Build your profile
scenes.visual: Screen recording of this worksheet, added in post-production.
scenes.narration: Today, create your Founder Profile. Name the people you are curious about, describe what you have noticed, and choose a realistic weekly commitment. If you have no idea yet, decide what you will observe.

scenes.title: Take one small step
scenes.visual: Founder closes notebook, walks into a bright community workspace.
scenes.narration: Ask yourself what might be wrong about your assumptions, and what would change your mind. Then choose one action for the next seven days. Progress begins with an honest starting point and a small step you can take.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: You can begin before you have an idea.

children: Entrepreneurship means finding a problem people care about, testing a way to solve it, and building a business that can keep delivering that value. A founder makes decisions under uncertainty. You do not need to know every answer; you need a way to learn.
By the end, you can
Explain what a founder actually does.
Connect your experience to a problem space.
Separate an observation from an assumption.
Set a realistic learning commitment.
Three useful words
Venture:
a business you are trying to build.
Assumption:
something you believe but have not yet tested.
Evidence:
something observed or collected that helps you check a belief.
A simple example

An event coordinator notices that visitors struggle to reconnect with people after an event. “People want an app” is an assumption. “Three visitors asked for a way to find someone they met” is an observation. The next step is to understand their experience before choosing a solution.
LYNQ was built in Dubai with a global outlook. Bring your own context: an everyday challenge in a shop, school, workplace, community, or event can be a starting point.
Your task today

Make a honest starting snapshot. “I’m not sure yet” is acceptable for your idea. Be specific about your motivation, skills, available time, and the people you would like to understand. This is a learning baseline, not an investor pitch.
Use short, concrete answers. Arabic entries are supported with automatic text direction. Avoid personal identifiers, confidential client details, or sensitive information.
Local storage is not encrypted. Anyone using this browser profile may access this draft. Download a copy before changing browsers; private browsing or browser cleanup can remove it.
Simulated Coach · no AI connection
Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.

replies.teach: A founder discovers a problem, learns from people, and decides what to test next. Your profile gives you a starting point; it is not a promise to build a product.
replies.guide: Start with one experience you know well. Who do you interact with? What frustrates them? Write an observation, then choose a small action for this week.

sections.label: 05 / CHALLENGE
sections.heading: Be curious about what could be wrong.

children: A red-team review looks for weak assumptions so you can improve your plan. It is not a judgment of your potential.
More questions to discuss
Are you interested in a customer's problem or only in your solution?
Can you reach the people you want to help?
Which skill is missing, and how can you learn or find support?
What would make you pause or choose a different problem?
Answer all three. You can retry; all three correct are required for local completion.
